criteria.evidence: All five sections (What it does, Inputs / Outputs, Rules & behavior, Acceptance criteria, Out of scope) are substantive; e.g. 'A cart with no items is never abandoned, even if it once held items...' and nine Given/When/Then criteria.
'A cart counts as ordered only through the order's own link to that cart... because matching carts by their contents would be a guess, and a wrong guess would hide a real lost cart from the owner.'

Rules are discrete bullets describing behavior, not a user story; acceptance is 'Given a cart with two items and no order, when it has been untouched for the abandonment window, then it is marked abandoned...'

Parent capability only says 'deciding which of a shop's carts count as abandoned'; the child adds the abandoned-at formula, failed-payment handling, cart A/cart B case, guest carts and stale-record behavior.

'Decides, for every cart in a shop, whether it is abandoned, and if so the moment it became abandoned.' The what, why (stop chasing buyers, avoid under-reporting) and edges (Out of scope names each neighbour) are all stated; the window length is explicitly flagged as pending an owner answer.
